properties.name: Every one-shot mode resolves its design before it opens one, and every flag is honoured or refused (step 1 of the --call door plan)
properties.rationale: THE CAUSE, walked in fact:root-cause-one-shot-modes-return-before-the-pointer-check-and-opening-a-store-creates-it-2026-10-02 and confirmed on main 9ecb405 by tests observed failing there: which rules a run obeyed was decided by WHERE its branch sat in main()'s chain of early returns, and the store opener creates a missing store. The pointer check, the --only-if-present check and every serve-time flag (--read-only, --export-to, --remote, --shared) sat below the one-shot branches, so a guard added for one entry point protected only the branches below it. The same class produced fact:call-ignores-read-only-and-the-write-lands-2026-10-02, fact:root-cause-call-accepts-export-to-and-never-reads-it-2026-10-02 and the --remote/--shared drops in fact:root-cause-the-door-opens-the-store-itself-and-never-reads-the-shared-servers-rendezvous-2026-10-02. THE FIX IS A POSITION, NOT A CHECK PER BRANCH: both steps run before the first early return, and the table refuses by default, so a flag added later cannot arrive silently ignored. The read/write split is the door's existing one (the served read_only_hint), not a second list. --read-only had a second hole the triage named (fact:root-cause-one-regex-cannot-separate-door-reads-because-the-read-set-is-not-in-the-command-and-not-served-2026-10-02): export_graph and export_surface are annotated read-only because they do not write the GRAPH, so write_lock never saw them and any read-only server wrote a file at a caller's path; the guard is now set by into_read_only and a unit test holds every file write in src/tools/ to it. A snapshot copy (into_snapshot_copy) keeps writing the file a caller asks for. DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT: forwarding a one-shot call (dec:idea-a-one-shot-call-reaches-the-design-where-it-is-served, open); honouring --export-to (req:a-writing-call-keeps-the-committed-export-current, step 2); the serving modes' own flags (a refusal at server start would leave an MCP client with no server and no reason) — where --read-only measurably fails (see the finding recorded with this change); design_identity creating a store on an empty path (it is marked a writer; the read-only identity call is a recorded follow-up in pointer.rs). BOUND OF THE CLAIM: --read-only changes no node, edge or property and writes no file at a caller's path; opening an existing store still does RocksDB's own housekeeping and refreshes the stamp, handshake record and usage ledger beside it (measured: WAL flushed to SSTs, LOG/MANIFEST/OPTIONS rotated). Governed by dec:idea-the-call-door-becomes-a-supported-harness-for-an-agent-that-cannot-use-mcp.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: main() now runs two steps FIRST, once, for every one-shot mode (one_shot.rs). gate: each mode names the command-line flags it reads; any other flag is refused by name with the mode, exit 1, and two modes are refused together. resolve_design: before --call, --export, --export-snapshot, --diff BASE or --import opens the store, a folder whose .reflow2.toml names a design on a server is refused with its id and address (nothing created, a leftover store not opened); --read-only refuses a write and creates nothing; --only-if-present is honoured; a read never creates a design (except in an opted-in folder). --read-only now means changes nothing in the design and writes no file: --call opens the service read-only, and into_read_only sets a file-write guard export_graph and export_surface pass, so a read-only SERVER no longer writes files either. --export-to and --remote/--shared with --call are refused naming step 2 and the open question. The installer (reflow2_init.py ensure_design_record) makes .reflow2/ before its minting export, since --export now creates a store only where a folder opted in.
